$comment: Authoritative cases for the blind-agent coverage self-report - `ui coverage` and the verdict every `act tap --point` carries - read by BOTH the Kotlin (reticle-core ScreenCoverageContractTest) and Swift (ReticleProtocol ScreenCoverageContractTests) suites, so the Android helper and the iOS host cannot answer 'how much of this screen is unreachable?' two ways. Each case is a snapshot plus the exact `ui coverage` lines and the exact per-point verdicts. What the cases pin: a coordinate over a node that HAD a selector is reported as an unnecessary fallback, naming the flag that would have worked (test id, then resource id, then css, then label, then ref); a coordinate over a named boundary is reported as justified, naming the boundary and its host node; a coordinate over captured-but-inert content and one over nothing captured are different answers; a point outside the screen says so instead of reading as empty; the grid sampling and the cell size are stated in the output rather than hidden in it; and inert/empty cells are counted apart from gaps, because without pixels a paragraph of text and a control the projection failed to mark are the same observation. Case four is the measurement that reshaped the rule: a hybrid screen read as 100% addressable because the WebView itself is tappable and carries an id, so a screen-sized container is now judged as scenery rather than as cover. Case five pins the other half of a tap's honesty: WHO receives the touch. A point can be perfectly addressable and still unreachable - the IME, a window above the target, or a node drawn over it takes the touch while the tap reports settled=1 - so every tap now carries an obstruction verdict, and the quiet cases (nothing in the way, and a screen-sized overlay container, which is scenery rather than an obstruction) are pinned too, because a warning that fires on an ordinary tap is one nobody reads.

cases.name: a coordinate over an addressable node is an unnecessary fallback, and the hint names the most stable handle each node has
report: coverage: 128x128, sampled on a 4x4 grid of 32px cells
addressable: 6 of 6 touch-relevant cell(s) (100%)
unreachable: none — every touch-relevant cell has an addressable node over it
inert: 10 cell(s) — a node is captured there, none of it interactive
empty: 0 cell(s) — no captured node contains the point
(inert and empty cells are NOT counted as gaps: without pixels, plain content and a control the projection failed to mark are the same observation)

points.warning: --point was not needed at (32,16): --test-id pay resolves to b1 (button), whose frame contains this point and would tap (32,16). A selector tap re-resolves and confirms its target; a coordinate does neither

--point was not needed at (96,16): --label "Next" resolves to t1 (button), whose frame contains this point and would tap (96,16). A selector tap re-resolves and confirms its target; a coordinate does neither

--point was not needed at (32,48): --css '#pay' resolves to d1 (textField), whose frame contains this point and would tap (32,48). A selector tap re-resolves and confirms its target; a coordinate does neither
no semantic selector covers (100,100) — no-interactive-node: the topmost node here is w1 (window) and it is not interactive, so no selector aims at this point
no semantic selector covers (200,10) — off-screen: this point is outside the 128x128 screen

cases.name: a cross-origin frame and a capped DOM walk each justify the coordinate by name, and the gap rows carry the host rects
report: coverage: 128x128, sampled on a 4x4 grid of 32px cells
addressable: 0 of 16 touch-relevant cell(s) (0%)
unreachable: 16 cell(s)
dom:capped(1500) wv [0,64 128x64] 8 cell(s)
iframe:cross-origin f1 [0,0 128x64] 8 cell(s)
inert: 0 cell(s) — a node is captured there, none of it interactive
empty: 0 cell(s) — no captured node contains the point
(inert and empty cells are NOT counted as gaps: without pixels, plain content and a control the projection failed to mark are the same observation)

points.warning: no semantic selector covers (64,32) — iframe:cross-origin: the frame at f1 is cross-origin, so its document is unreadable by browser policy — coordinates are the only path into it
no semantic selector covers (64,96) — dom:capped(1500): the DOM walk under wv stopped at its node cap (1500 node(s) captured), so nodes here were never captured at all — narrow the page or scroll

cases.name: a self-drawn wheel, the area outside every node, and the keyboard's own rows are three different answers
report: coverage: 128x128, sampled on a 4x4 grid of 32px cells
addressable: 0 of 2 touch-relevant cell(s) (0%)
unreachable: 2 cell(s)
wheel wheel1 [0,0 64x32] 2 cell(s)
inert: 7 cell(s) — a node is captured there, none of it interactive
empty: 3 cell(s) — no captured node contains the point
keyboard: 4 cell(s) covered by the IME (another process's window)
(inert and empty cells are NOT counted as gaps: without pixels, plain content and a control the projection failed to mark are the same observation)

points.warning: no semantic selector covers (32,16) — wheel: wheel1 is a wheel column whose candidate values exist only as pixels — drive it with `act swipe`
no semantic selector covers (112,16) — nothing-captured: no captured node contains this point

cases.name: a screen-sized tappable container is not cover: the cells inside it with nothing smaller captured are the gap
report: coverage: 128x128, sampled on a 4x4 grid of 32px cells
addressable: 1 of 16 touch-relevant cell(s) (6%)
unreachable: 15 cell(s)
container-only wv [0,0 128x128] 15 cell(s)
inert: 0 cell(s) — a node is captured there, none of it interactive
empty: 0 cell(s) — no captured node contains the point
(inert and empty cells are NOT counted as gaps: without pixels, plain content and a control the projection failed to mark are the same observation)

points.warning: --point was not needed at (16,16): --test-id ok resolves to b1 (button), whose frame contains this point and would tap (16,16). A selector tap re-resolves and confirms its target; a coordinate does neither

no semantic selector covers (100,100) — container-only: the only addressable node here is wv (webView), a screen-sized container whose own tap point is (64,64) — nothing smaller is captured at this point

cases.name: a tap is warned when something else receives the touch: the IME, a window above the target, or a node drawn over it — and a screen-sized overlay container is scenery, not an obstruction
report: coverage: 128x128, sampled on a 4x4 grid of 32px cells
addressable: 4 of 12 touch-relevant cell(s) (33%)
unreachable: 8 cell(s)
container-only scenery [0,0 128x128] 8 cell(s)
inert: 0 cell(s) — a node is captured there, none of it interactive
empty: 0 cell(s) — no captured node contains the point
keyboard: 4 cell(s) covered by the IME (another process's window)
(inert and empty cells are NOT counted as gaps: without pixels, plain content and a control the projection failed to mark are the same observation)

obstructions.warning: the touch at (16,16) may not reach the target — occluded:node: icon (image) is drawn over pay at this point and is itself interactive, so it consumes the touch
the touch at (64,48) may not reach the target — occluded:window: a window above beneath covers this point (w2) — the touch lands in that window, not on the target
the touch at (32,112) may not reach the target — occluded:keyboard: the IME covers this point, so the touch goes to the keyboard and not to the app — dismiss it with `act hide-keyboard` first
